:module.eks_blueprints_kubernetes_addons: explicit depends_on of :resource.aws_s3_object.this is redundant — already implied by attribute references

module.eks_blueprints_kubernetes_addons already depends on :resource.aws_s3_object.this implicitly: the spark_history_server_helm_config values interpolate ${aws_s3_object.this.key} (and aws_s3_bucket.this.id), which the graph captures as an implicit_dep. Listing aws_s3_object.this in the module's depends_on duplicates that existing ordering and can be removed.

aws_eks_node_group.managed_ng already references aws_iam_role.managed_ng via node_role_arn = aws_iam_role.managed_ng[0].arn, so the dependency is established implicitly. Including aws_iam_role.managed_ng in depends_on is redundant.

null_resource.update_trust_policy's local-exec command already interpolates ${aws_iam_role.emr_on_eks_execution.id}, which establishes an implicit dependency on aws_iam_role.emr_on_eks_execution. Listing it in depends_on is redundant.

null_resource.update_trust_policy's local-exec command already interpolates ${kubernetes_namespace.spark.id}, which establishes an implicit dependency on kubernetes_namespace.spark. Listing it in depends_on is redundant.

kubernetes_role_binding.team bind's to role_ref.name = "${each.key}-role", a literal string, so Terraform has no dependency on kubernetes_role.team. The binding should be created after the Role it references. Add an explicit depends_on (or reference kubernetes_role.team metadata name).

kubernetes_cluster_role_binding.team references role_ref.name = "${each.key}-team-cluster-role", a literal string, creating no ordering against kubernetes_cluster_role.team. The ClusterRoleBinding should be applied after the ClusterRole exists.

kubernetes_role_binding.emr_containers sets role_ref.name = local.emr_service_name (a literal), so there is no dependency on kubernetes_role.emr_containers even though the binding references that Role. Order the RoleBinding after the Role.

kubernetes_role_binding_v1.adot uses role_ref.name = local.eks_addon_role_name (a literal string) and only depends on var.enable_amazon_eks_adot, so nothing orders it after kubernetes_role_v1.adot which defines that Role. Add ordering so the Role exists first.

kubernetes_cluster_role_binding_v1.adot uses role_ref.name = local.eks_addon_clusterrole_name (a literal string) and does not depend on kubernetes_cluster_role_v1.adot, which defines that ClusterRole. The binding should be applied after the ClusterRole.
